stage: Later - RECORDED ONLY, explicitly after the iOS work is finished
description: An Android .apk alongside the iOS .ipa. The user stated this directly and framed the ordering themselves, twice. Their words the second time: they want the .apk for Android users once the iOS side is done, they will update the .ipa more often because iOS is their own device, and they will still update the .apk occasionally. Nothing here is to be built now. It is recorded because the decision changes a written project rule, and because a surprising amount of the work is already done.
last_reviewed: 2026-09-21, after the settings, rewind, controller and web-removal work

decision_point.question: A second platform contradicts a steering rule that is currently written as non-negotiable.
decision_point.detail: .kiro/steering/product-scope.md opens with 'the .ipa is the only deliverable' and states that the project is NOT dual-platform. That rule exists to stop effort leaking into the browser build, which was scaffolding. An Android target is a different proposition from keeping a PWA alive, but it does contradict the letter of that document. The steering file now carries an 'Android is a real future deliverable, and it is not a PWA' section acknowledging this, so the contradiction is documented rather than latent.
decision_point.recommendation: When this work actually starts, tighten the opening line of product-scope.md in the SAME change so the document does not argue with itself. Keep the anti-web rule absolutely intact: Android means a native Kotlin shell over the same Rust engine, and it is never a reason to revive a browser build. Until then iOS remains the only target, exactly as the user said.

what_already_exists: UniFFI generates Kotlin bindings from the SAME #[uniffi::export] annotations that produce the Swift facade. The engine's public API would not have to change at all. That surface is now considerably larger and more useful than when this was first recorded: launch, tick, save and load state, cheats, core options, input, audio drain and output rate, volume and mute, scale mode, filter, speed, and the whole rewind tape are all described in a binding-neutral way.

Everything added since this record was written went into RUST rather than Swift, deliberately and for this reason. Volume is the worked example: it is applied in EmulatorBridge::drain_audio rather than on the iOS mixer, so Android inherits it for free instead of reimplementing it. The same is true of the rewind tape, the fast-forward audio resampling, and the preference persistence inside the bridge that survives a session change. The steering file now states this as a rule.

The graphics layer is wgpu, which already targets Vulkan on Android. The Apple-specific part is narrow: gfx/metal.rs and the MTLDevice ownership rule. Renderer::from_surface is explicitly written against a surface rather than against Metal, and its doc comment now says that is so the next backend is a configuration change. Everything else in gfx/renderer.rs, including the letterboxing, the integer scale maths, the two samplers and the capture path, is platform-neutral.

ALL input mapping lives in Rust on purpose, and the per-source merge is now exercised rather than theoretical: iOS drives the touch layer and the gamepad layer simultaneously through apply_gamepad_from, so a Kotlin front end has a working example of the contract rather than an untested capability.

scripts/build-core.sh has a per-platform subcommand namespace (ios <core>, ios-all, ios-names). An android <core> namespace follows the established pattern rather than inventing one. Note the script is now iOS-only and about 550 lines, since the WASM half was deleted, so there is more room and a clearer template than there was.

The frame pacer, audio resampler, core registry, pixel conversion and rewind tape are pure Rust with no platform dependency and are covered by the existing cargo test suites (85 default, 95 with features).
what_is_genuinely_new: A Kotlin or Jetpack Compose shell: library, player, settings, the touch controls and the layout editor. This is the bulk of it, and it is now a larger job than when first recorded because the iOS UI has grown: cover art with a chooser, the detail sheet, the import flow, the settings screen with picture, sound, speed, rewind and controller sections, and the control layout editor.

Rebuilding all five libretro cores for aarch64-linux-android with the NDK. Each core's makefile has an android platform target, but they are not the ios-arm64 ones and each needs the same per-core reading the iOS builds needed.
An Android surface attach path in gfx/, plus deciding whether Vulkan or GLES is the floor.

Audio OUTPUT only, not the audio engine. This entry used to say audio was written for neither platform; that is no longer true. The engine side is done and platform-neutral: drain_audio, set_output_sample_rate, audio_stats, flush_audio, volume and mute are all exported, and the resampler reconciles the core's rate with whatever the device reports. What Android needs is an AAudio or Oboe consumer plus its own lock-free ring, which is the AudioOutput.swift half. Read that file's header first: the reason the render callback must not touch the engine Mutex is a property of real-time audio, not of iOS, and it applies identically on Android.
A CI runner story. iOS needs macOS and Android does not, so an Android job is the easier half and could run on the existing Linux runners.

Distribution: an .apk can be installed directly, so the sideloading and entitlements machinery has no Android counterpart and none is needed. Do not name a specific iOS installer in any shared documentation; the owner does not use TrollStore.
carry_over_from_this_task: The input contract applies verbatim on Android and the traps are the same. apply_gamepad_from takes the W3C standard gamepad order (0 B, 1 A, 2 Y, 3 X, 4 L, 5 R, 6 L2, 7 R2, 8 Select, 9 Start, 10 L3, 11 R3, 12 Up, 13 Down, 14 Left, 15 Right) and NOT libretro's joypad order. It REPLACES the named source layer wholesale, so it must be pushed every frame, and the on-screen pad and any physical controller must use DIFFERENT layers or the quiet one erases the other. Axes want Y negative for up, with the deadzone at 0.35, and the engine synthesises D-pad presses from the left stick so the front end must not. The per-system button mappings read from the upstream cores (Mega Drive A B C are retro Y B A; Master System and Game Gear 1 and 2 are retro B and A; PS1 Cross Circle Square Triangle are retro B A Y X) are properties of the cores, not of iOS. A Kotlin front end should port native/ios/TouchControls.swift's PadSlot table and D-pad surface maths rather than re-deriving either, and native/ios/PhysicalControllers.swift's header explains why polling once per frame beats per-button callbacks against this engine.
findings: Recorded, not planned in detail and not built, because the user was explicit twice that it comes after the iOS work and that iOS is what they will update most. The cheapest thing that can be done for it now is being done continuously and costs nothing: put new behaviour in the Rust engine rather than in Swift, because anything left in Swift is work Android pays for a second time. The browser build has now been deleted, which removes the one thing this record used to warn about: an eventual Android target must still never become an argument for reviving a web build, because a Kotlin shell over this engine and a web page are entirely different things.
